R032.title: Threshold conjecture for proper bosonic atomic ground states
R032.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$ be the number of bosonic electrons, let $Z>0$ be the nuclear charge, and let $Z_*(N)$ denote the infimum of charges that properly bind $N$ bosonic electrons. Write $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ for an $N$-body ground-state wave function of the Coulomb Hamiltonian.

**Threshold conjecture.** A proper $N$-body ground-state wave function $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ exists whenever $Z>Z_*(N)$.

By definition, a ground state at $Z=Z_*(N)$ need not be proper, so the conjecture concerns the entire strict-binding region above the threshold. It is presented as an analogue of a claim discussed by Reed and Simon; the available context does not establish the conjecture's resolution.
R032.source_name: Michael K. -H. Kiessling, “The Hartree limit of Born's ensemble for the ground state of a bosonic atom or ion”, arXiv:1204.2511 (2012).
R032.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.2511

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2012). “I thank the referee for drawing my attention to this conjecture, which is mentioned as an open problem in Chpt.12 of .”

R032.title: Monotonic binding conjecture for bosonic electron numbers
R032.statement:
Let $Z>0$ be a nuclear charge, let $N_{\mathrm{max}}(Z)$ be the maximum number of bosonic electrons that a nucleus of charge $Z$ can bind, and write $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ for a proper $N$-body ground-state wave function of the Coulomb Hamiltonian.

**Monotonic binding conjecture.** A proper $N$-body ground-state wave function $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ exists for every integer $N$ satisfying

$$
1\leq N\leq N_{\mathrm{max}}(Z).
$$

Equivalently, if the nucleus binds $N$ electrons, it also binds every smaller positive number of electrons. This is stated as an open problem in the cited literature and is known from Zhislin's theorem only in the range $N<Z+2$.

R032.title: Hohenberg–Kohn conjecture for density-potential determination
R032.statement:
Let $X$ be the density space, let $X^*$ be its dual space of external potentials, let $\mathcal{D}^N$ denote the set of $N$-particle densities, and let ${\underline{\partial}}F[\rho]$ be the relevant subdifferential of the universal functional $F$ at $\rho$. A density is a ground-state density for a potential when it arises as a ground state of the corresponding external-potential Hamiltonian.

**Hohenberg–Kohn conjecture.** For every $\rho\in\mathcal{D}^N$, either

$$
{\underline{\partial}} F[\rho] = \{ -v + \mu \mid \mu \in \mathbb{R} \}
$$

for some $v\in X^*$, or

$$
{\underline{\partial}} F[\rho] = \emptyset,
$$

whenever there are no potentials for which $\rho$ is a ground-state density. Thus, whenever the density is $v$-representable, it determines the potential up to an additive constant.

The conjecture is the rigorous form of the Hohenberg–Kohn density-as-basic-variable principle in density functional theory. Its original proof has a non-rigorous pointwise division by the wavefunction, and it remains partially open for general potentials $v\in X^*$; unique continuation is known for, among others, suitable locally integrable potentials including Coulomb potentials.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.05268

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

R032.title: Bounded Excess Electrons
R032.statement: For the $N$-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with nuclear charge $Z$, let $N_0(Z)$ be the least $N$ after which adding electrons no longer lowers the ground-state energy. Prove that $N_0(Z)-Z$ remains bounded as $Z\to\infty$.

R032.title: Asymptotics of Atomic Ionization Energy
R032.statement: For the $N$-electron Coulomb ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$, determine the asymptotics of the ionization energy $\delta E(Z)=E(Z,Z-1)-E(Z,Z)$ as $Z\to\infty$.

R032.title: Stability of matter for Coulomb molecules with fermionic electrons
R032.statement:
For a molecule with $M$ nuclei of equal charge $+Z$ at positions $R_1,\c\c,R_M\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $N$ electrons, let
$$
H=-\sum_{j=1}^N\Delta_j+W(X),
$$
where
$$
W(X)=\sum_{j=1}^N V(x_j)+\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\frac1{|x_i-x_j|}+U,
$$
$$
V(x)=-Z\sum_{j=1}^M\frac1{|x-R_j|},\qquad
U=Z^2\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq M}\frac1{|R_i-R_j|}.
$$
With the electronic Hilbert space restricted to antisymmetric wavefunctions, the ground-state energy
$$
E=\inf\{(\psi,H\psi):\|\psi\|_2=1\}
$$
is bounded below, for large $N$ and $M$, by $-A(Z)(N+M)$ for a constant $A(Z)$ depending only on $Z$. The report states that this stability-of-matter assertion was proved by Dyson and Lenard.

R033.title: Replica symmetry breaking condition for indefinite multi-species Sherrington–Kirkpatrick models
R033.statement:
Let the multi-species Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model have an indefinite interaction matrix $\boldsymbol{D}^2$, and let $\boldsymbol{C}$, $\boldsymbol{C}'$, $\boldsymbol{L}$ and $\boldsymbol{93}'$ denote the matrices defined by the replica-symmetric solution. Write $\rho$ for the spectral radius, $\operatorname{spec}$ for the spectrum, and $\Re$ for the real part of an eigenvalue. **Replica symmetry breaking condition.** For general indefinite $\boldsymbol{D}^2$, if

$$
\beta^2\max\left\{\rho(\boldsymbol{C}\boldsymbol{D}^2\boldsymbol{L}),\max_{\lambda\in \operatorname{spec}(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}'\boldsymbol{D}^2\boldsymbol{L})} \Re(\lambda)\right\}>1,
$$

the system is in the replica symmetry breaking phase. This proposes the boundary of the replica-symmetric regime for indefinite interaction matrices; the preceding bipartite example gives evidence for the condition, but the general assertion is not established in the supplied text.

R033.title: Critical-temperature variance conjecture for the SK model
R033.statement:
Let $F_N^{SK}(\beta)$ denote the free energy of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with system size $N$ at inverse temperature $\beta$, and let the critical value be $\beta_c=1$. **Critical-temperature variance conjecture.** At the critical value, one expects

$$
\operatorname{Var}(F_N^{SK}(\beta_c))=\frac{1}{6}N^{-2}\log N+O(N^{-2}),\qquad\text{as }N\to\infty.
$$

This conjecture concerns the fluctuation scale of the SK free energy at the transition between the high- and low-temperature regimes; numerical computations and heuristic arguments support it, while the stated asymptotic remains unproved in the source.

R033.title: Polynomial runtime scaling conjecture for reluctant dynamics in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
R033.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a “sufficiently nice” probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\mathbb{E}_{X \sim \mu}X=0$ and $\mathbb{E}_{X \sim \mu}X^2=1$, let $\lambda\in[0,+\infty]$, and suppose that $\sqrt{N}\cdot J$ has i.i.d. entries distributed as $\mu$. Let $T=T(N,\mu,\lambda)$ be the random runtime of reluctant dynamics on an $N\times N$ random matrix $J$. **Polynomial runtime scaling conjecture.** There exist constants $\alpha=\alpha(\mu,\lambda)>0$ and $\beta=\beta(\mu,\lambda)>0$ such that

$$
\frac{T(N,\mu,\lambda)}{\alpha(\mu,\lambda)N^{\beta(\mu,\lambda)}}\to 1
$$

in probability as $N\to\infty$. This strengthens prior evidence for polynomial runtime scaling in the classical Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with Gaussian entries to sufficiently nice entry distributions more generally; the statement remains conjectural.

R033.title: Universality conjecture for greedy dynamics runtime exponents
R033.statement: Let $\mu$ be a “sufficiently nice” probability measure with mean $0$ and variance $1$, and let $\beta(\mu,0)$ denote the scaling exponent of the runtime of $0$-reluctant, or greedy, dynamics. **Greedy runtime universality conjecture.** $\beta(\mu,0)\approx 1.1$ is a constant independent of $\mu$. This conjecture proposes universality of the greedy runtime exponent across a broad class of normalized entry distributions; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

R033.title: Universality conjecture for positive-discrepancy entry distributions
R033.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure with mean $0$ and variance $1$, and define its discrepancy by

$$
\Delta(\mu)=\inf_{n\geq 1}\inf_{x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu),\ s_1,\ldots,s_n\in\{\pm1\}}\left|\sum_{i=1}^n s_i x_i\right|.
$$

Let $\beta(\mu,\infty)$ denote the scaling exponent of the runtime of $\infty$-reluctant dynamics. **Positive-discrepancy universality conjecture.** $\beta(\mu,\infty)\approx 1.6$ is a constant independent of $\mu$ for any “sufficiently nice” $\mu$ with mean $0$, variance $1$, and discrepancy $\Delta(\mu)>0$. This identifies positive-discrepancy distributions as a proposed universality class for the runtime exponent, but the claim remains conjectural.

R033.title: Non-universality conjecture for zero-discrepancy entry distributions
R033.statement: Let $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ be probability measures with mean $0$ and variance $1$, and let $\Delta(\mu)$ be the discrepancy of a probability measure. Let $\beta(\mu,\infty)$ denote the runtime scaling exponent of $\infty$-reluctant dynamics. **Zero-discrepancy non-universality conjecture.** There exist $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3$ such that $\Delta(\mu_1)>0$, $\Delta(\mu_2)=\Delta(\mu_3)=0$, and the three numbers $\beta(\mu_1,\infty)$, $\beta(\mu_2,\infty)$, and $\beta(\mu_3,\infty)$ are all distinct. This predicts that positive-discrepancy distributions and zero-discrepancy distributions do not share one universal runtime exponent, while the conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

R033.title: Aspelmeier's critical variance conjecture for the SK free energy
R033.statement:
Let $F_{N,\beta}$ denote the free energy of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with system size $N$ and inverse temperature $\beta$. At the critical temperature, $\beta=1$.

**Aspelmeier's conjecture.** The variance satisfies

$$
{\mathsf{Var}}(F_{N,\beta=1})=\frac16\log N+O(1).
$$

This prediction was obtained using non-rigorous physics methods and concerns the fluctuation scale at the phase transition. It has since been confirmed in the paper: the critical variance has logarithmic growth with the stated leading constant.

R036.title: Hausel–Letellier–Villegas conjecture for character varieties
R036.statement:
Let ${\bm \mu}=(\mu^1,\ldots,\mu^k)\in{\mathcal{P}_n}^k$ be a tuple of partitions, let ${\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu}$ be the corresponding $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ character variety of a genus-$g$ Riemann surface with $k$ punctures, and let

$$
d_{\bm \mu}:=n^2(2g-2+k)-\sum_{i,j}(\mu_j^i)^2+2.
$$

Write $H_c({\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu};x,y,t)$ for its compactly supported mixed Hodge polynomial and define $H_c({\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu};q,t):=H_c({\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu};\sqrt q,\sqrt q,t)$. **Hausel–Letellier–Villegas conjecture.** The polynomial $H_c({\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu};x,y,t)$ depends only on $xy$ and $t$, and

$$
H_c({\mathcal{M}}_{\bm \mu};q,t)=(t\sqrt q)^{d_{\bm \mu}}\;\mathbb{H}_{\bm \mu}\left(-{\frac 1{\sqrt q}},t\sqrt q\right).
$$

This conjecture generalizes the corresponding conjecture for the varieties ${\mathcal{M}}_n$ and passes several consistency checks, including the cases $k=1$, $\mu^1=(n)$ and $g=0$, $k=2$. Its symmetry implies the associated curious Poincaré duality, while the general mixed-Hodge-polynomial identity remains unresolved in the source.
R036.source_name: T. Hausel, E. Letellier and F. Rodriguez-Villegas, “Arithmetic harmonic analysis on character and quiver varieties”, arXiv:0810.2076 (2011).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.2076

R036.title: Periodic stability for homology of mapping-class-group congruence subgroups
R036.statement: Let $\operatorname{Mod}_{g,1}(p)$ be the level-$p$ congruence subgroup of the mapping class group of a genus-$g$ surface with one boundary component. Its integral homology carries an action of $\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{F}_p)$. **Modular periodic stability conjecture.** For every $i\geq 0$ and every prime $p$, the sequence $\{H_1(\operatorname{Mod}_{g,1}(p);\mathbb{Z})\}$ of $\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{F}_p)$-representations is uniformly stably periodic with period $p$. The immediately preceding theorem establishes this assertion for $i=1$ in the stated formulation, while the conjectural extension remains unresolved in the source.

R036.title: Vanishing conjecture for the top cohomology of $\operatorname{SL}_n\mathbb{Z}$
R036.statement: Let $\operatorname{SL}_n\mathbb{Z}$ be the special linear group over the integers, and let $H^*(-;\mathbb{Q})$ denote rational group cohomology. **Vanishing conjecture.** $H^{\binom{n}{2}-i}(\operatorname{SL}_n\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{Q})=0$ for all $i<n-1$. This vanishing is presented as a consequence of the proposed stable instability and reflects torsion phenomena in the arithmetic group; the source gives no resolution.

R036.title: Parity stability conjecture for the top cohomology of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$
R036.statement: Let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n\geq 2$, let $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ be its automorphism group, and let $H^*(-;\mathbb{Q})$ denote rational group cohomology. **Parity stability conjecture.** For each $i\geq 0$ the group $H^{2n-2-i}(\operatorname{Aut}(F_n);\mathbb{Q})$ only depends on the parity of $n$ for $n\gg i$. This is a more speculative analogue of the stable instability conjectures for arithmetic and mapping class groups, and the source states that it remains open even for $i=0$.

R036.title: Nonvanishing signature conjecture for quantum representations
R036.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p\geq 5$, let $\zeta$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity, and define

$$
A_p=(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}\exp\left(\frac{(p+1)\pi i}{2p}\right)
$$

for odd $p$, and $A_p=\pm\exp\left(\frac{\pi i}{p}\right)$ for even $p$. Assume that neither $\zeta$ nor $\overline{\zeta}$ equals $A_p$. **Nonvanishing signature conjecture.** For all $g$ in some arithmetic progression, the signature $\sigma(g,\zeta)$ of the corresponding Hermitian form is nonzero modulo $p$:

$$
\sigma(g,\zeta)\not\equiv 0 \pmod p.
$$

The claim is presented as evidence-based motivation for further study of signatures of quantum representations; the source does not provide a resolution, so its status remains open.
R036.source_name: Louis Funar and Wolfgang Pitsch, “Images of quantum representations of mapping class groups and Dupont-Guichardet-Wigner quasi-homomorphisms”, arXiv:1209.0302 (2015).

R036.title: The finite-volume conjecture for outer space
R036.statement: Let $X_n$ be outer space, let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ act on it naturally, and let $ds^2$ and $ds^2_{\varepsilon}$ be the two Riemannian metrics defined in the previous section. The quotient $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)\backslash X_n$ is equipped with the corresponding quotient Riemannian volume. **The finite-volume conjecture.** The volume of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)\backslash X_n$ with respect to either of the Riemannian metrics $ds^2$ and $ds^2_{\varepsilon}$ is finite. This conjecture is motivated by the finite-volume quotients arising for mapping class groups and arithmetic groups; the source gives no resolution.

R036.title: The torsion-translate conjecture for local-system jump loci of hypersurface singularity complements
R036.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb{C}^n$, let $f:X\to\mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic, let $x\in f^{-1}(0)$, and for a sufficiently small ball $B_x$ centered at $x$ set

$$
U_{f,x}=B_x\cap\bigl(X\setminus f^{-1}(0)\bigr).
$$

Thus $U_{f,x}$ is the complement of a hypersurface singularity germ, and let $\mathcal{M}_{\textrm{B}}(U_{f,x})$ be its rank-one character variety. **Torsion-translate conjecture.** The cohomology jump loci

$$
\Sigma^i_k\subset\mathcal{M}_{\textrm{B}}(U_{f,x})
$$

are finite unions of torsion translates of subtori. This predicts an arithmetic structure for the jump loci of local systems on hypersurface-singularity complements; the supplied text does not state a resolution.

R036.title: The integrality conjecture for character varieties
R036.statement:
Let $g,d\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, let $\Sigma_g$ be a genus-$g$ surface, and let $\operatorname{Rep}_d(\Sigma_g)$ denote the stack of $d$-dimensional representations of its fundamental group. Let $\overline{\operatorname{Rep}}_d^{\operatorname{\zeta}}(\Sigma_g)$ be the smooth quasiprojective variety of twisted representations modulo $\operatorname{PGL}_d$, and let $\mathbb{L}$ denote the Lefschetz mixed Hodge structure. Then the following holds as an isomorphism of $\mathbb{N}$-graded mixed Hodge structures:

**The integrality conjecture.**

$$
\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb{N}}\operatorname{H}_c\left(\operatorname{Rep}_d(\Sigma_g),\mathbb{Q}\right)\otimes\mathbb{L}^{\otimes(1-g)n^2}\cong \operatorname{Sym}\left(\bigoplus_{d\geq 1}\operatorname{H}_c\left(\overline{\operatorname{Rep}}_d^{\operatorname{\zeta}}(\Sigma_g),\mathbb{Q}\right)\otimes \operatorname{H}_c(\operatorname{pt}/\mathbb{C}^*,\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{L}^{\otimes(1-g)n^2}\right).
$$

This is the integrality conjecture attributed in the source to; it predicts that the compactly supported cohomology of the character stacks is freely generated, in the symmetric-algebra sense, by the cohomology of the twisted character varieties together with the cohomology of $\operatorname{pt}/\mathbb{C}^*$. The formula is known in genus one in the form described immediately before the conjecture, while the general case is presented as conjectural.
R036.source_name: Ben Davison, “The integrality conjecture and the cohomology of preprojective stacks”, arXiv:1602.02110 (2022).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.02110

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

R036.title: Twisted parabolic Higgs-moduli perverse Hodge polynomial conjecture
R036.statement:
Let $C$ be a complex smooth projective curve of genus $g$, with divisor $D=p_1+\dots+p_k+rp$, where the points are distinct and $p$ has multiplicity $r$. Let ${\bm \mu}$ be a $k$-tuple of partitions, let ${\mathcal{M}}_\Dol^{{\bm \mu},r}$ be the associated smooth moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles, and let $d_{{\bm \mu},r}$ be its dimension. Its perverse Hodge polynomial is

$$
PH({\mathcal{M}}_\Dol^{{\bm \mu},r};q,t)=\sum \dim\left(\operatorname{Gr}^P_i(H^k({\mathcal{M}}_\Dol^{{\bm \mu},r}))\right)q^it^k.
$$

Let $\mathbb{H}_{{\bm \mu},r}(z,w)$ denote the polynomial defined by the paper. **Perverse Hodge polynomial conjecture.** We expect

$$
PH({\mathcal{M}}_\Dol^{{\bm \mu},r};q,t)=(qt^2)^{d_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}}\mathbb{H}_{{\bm \mu},r}(q^{-1/2},-q^{1/2}t).
$$

The cited string-theoretical work gives evidence for this identity, while the source presents it as a mathematical conjecture rather than a proved result.
R036.source_name: Tamas Hausel, Martin Mereb and Michael Lennox Wong, “Arithmetic and representation theory of wild character varieties”, arXiv:1604.03382 (2016).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.03382

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2016).

R036.title: Wild character-variety mixed Hodge polynomial conjecture
R036.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}$ be the generic wild character variety, let $d_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}$ be its dimension, and let $\tilde{{\bm \mu}}=(\mu^1,\dots,\mu^k,(1^n),\dots,(1^n))$ with $r=r_1+\cdots+r_m$. Write $WH({\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}};q,t)$ for its mixed Hodge polynomial. **Wild character-variety conjecture.** We have

$$
WH({\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}};q,t)=(qt^2)^{d_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}}\mathbb{H}_{\tilde{{\bm \mu}},r}(q^{-1/2},-tq^{-1/2}).
$$

The paper proves the $t=-1$ specialization, so the conjecture extends that theorem to the full mixed Hodge polynomial. The source describes this as a conjectural partial answer to a problem concerning character varieties with matching mixed Hodge polynomials.
R036.source_name: Tamas Hausel, Martin Mereb and Michael Lennox Wong, “Arithmetic and representation theory of wild character varieties”, arXiv:1604.03382 (2016).

R036.title: Curious Poincaré duality for wild character varieties
R036.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}$ be the generic wild character variety, let $d_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}$ be its dimension, and let $WH({\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}};q,t)$ be its mixed Hodge polynomial. **Curious Poincaré duality conjecture.**

$$
WH({\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}};q,t)=(qt)^{d_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}}WH({\mathcal{M}}_\B^{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}};1/(qt^2),t).
$$

The identity is deduced formally in the paper from the preceding mixed-Hodge-polynomial conjecture and a symmetry of the polynomials $\mathbb{H}_{{\bm \mu},{\bf r}}$. Thus it remains conjectural to the extent that the preceding conjecture remains open.

R036.title: Combinatorial identity from a wild-to-tame character-variety correspondence
R036.statement:
Let $\mu\in\mathcal{P}_n$, let $\mu'$ be the partition obtained by deleting the first part of $\mu$, and let $n'=n-\mu_1$. Set

$$
{\bm \mu}'=((n'-1,1),\dots,(n'-1,1),\mu')\in\mathcal{P}_{n'}^{n+1}.
$$

Assuming the notation and the wild-to-tame correspondence in the preceding discussion, **wild-to-tame combinatorial conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{H}_{(\mu,(1^n)),1}(z,w)=\mathbb{H}_{{\bm \mu}'}(z,w).
$$

This identity follows in the source from combining Boalch's isomorphism between the relevant wild and tame character varieties with the preceding mixed-Hodge-polynomial conjecture. It is therefore presented as a conjectural combinatorial consequence, rather than an independent theorem.

R036.title: Integrality conjecture for logarithmic HLV kernels
R036.statement:
Let $\mathbb H_{u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_g}[X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n;q,t,T]$ be the logarithmic HLV kernel, and let $\mathbb H_{u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_g,\lambda}(q,t)$ denote the coefficient of $\mathbb H$ in front of the monomial

$$
\prod_{i=1}^n\prod_j X_{ij}^{\lambda^{(i)}_j}
$$

for a tuple of partitions $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)},\ldots,\lambda^{(n)})$. **Part 1.** For every such tuple $\lambda$,

$$
\mathbb H_{u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_g,\lambda}(q,t)\in\mathbb Z[q,t,u_1,\ldots,u_g,u_1^{-1},\ldots,u_g^{-1}].
$$

This is the integrality part of the HLV-kernel conjectures, formulated in connection with character varieties and moduli spaces of Higgs bundles. The supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.

R036.references:

R036.title: Perfectness conjecture for the closure of the compactly supported pure mapping class group
R036.statement:
Let $S$ be a surface of genus at least $3$. Write

$$
\overline{\mathrm{PMap}_c(S)}
$$

for the closure of the compactly supported pure mapping class group in the pure mapping class group of $S$.

**Perfectness conjecture.** The group $\overline{\mathrm{PMap}_c(S)}$ is perfect.

This conjecture generalizes the perfectness of pure mapping class groups of finite-type surfaces of genus at least $3$. Its relationship with the computation of the first cohomology of pure mapping class groups is discussed in the source, but no resolution is given there.
R036.source_name: Javier Aramayona, Priyam Patel and Nicholas G. Vlamis, “The first integral cohomology of pure mapping class groups”, arXiv:1711.03132 (2020).

R036.title: Integrality conjecture distinguishing pseudo-Anosov mapping tori
R036.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a compact oriented surface and let $f\in\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma)$ be pseudo-Anosov. Let

$$
M_f=\Sigma\times[0,1]/_{(x,1)\sim(f(x),0)}
$$

be the mapping torus of $f$, and let $TV_r(M_f)$ denote its $SO(3)$ Turaev–Viro invariant at odd level $r$. **Integrality conjecture.** If $f$ is pseudo-Anosov, then there can be at most finitely many odd integers $r$ such that

$$
TV_r(M_f)\in\mathbb{Z}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed to distinguish Turaev–Viro invariants of mapping tori of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes from those of periodic mapping classes. The paper proves the analogous finiteness conclusion under the hypothesis $lTV(M_f)>0$, but does not establish that hypothesis for every pseudo-Anosov mapping torus.
R036.source_name: Renaud Detcherry and Efstratia Kalfagianni, “Quantum representations and monodromies of fibered links”, arXiv:1711.03251 (2019).

R036.title: The word-measure rigidity conjecture for free groups
R036.statement: Let $\mathbf{F}_r$ be the free group of rank $r$, and let $w\in\mathbf{F}_r$ induce a probability measure on each compact group via its word map. **Word-measure rigidity conjecture.** If two words $w_{1},w_{2}\in\mathbf{F}_r$ induce the same measure on every compact group, then there exists $\phi\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf{F}_r)$ with $w_{2}=\phi(w_{1})$. This asks whether equality of word measures on all compact groups can occur only for words related by an automorphism of the free group; it was settled affirmatively by Puder and Parzanchevski using word measures on symmetric groups.
R036.source_name: Michael Magee and Doron Puder, “Matrix Group Integrals, Surfaces, and Mapping Class Groups I: U(n)”, arXiv:1802.04862 (2019).

R036.title: Tame purity conjecture for open de Rham spaces
R036.statement:
Let $\mathscr{M}_{\bm \mu}^*$ be the tame open de Rham space associated with a generic tuple of semisimple adjoint orbits, and let $\mathscr{M}_{\mathbf{B}}^{{\bm \mu}, \mathbf{r}}$ and $\mathscr{M}_{{\bm \mu}, \mathbf{r}}^*$ denote the corresponding character variety and open de Rham space with the indicated additional irregularity data. The Riemann–Hilbert map induces

$$
\nu_a^*: H^*(\mathscr{M}_{\mathbf{B}}^{{\bm \mu}, \mathbf{r}},\mathbb{Q})\to H^*(\mathscr{M}_{{\bm \mu}, \mathbf{r}}^*,\mathbb{Q}).
$$

**Purity conjecture.** The map $\nu_a^*$ preserves mixed Hodge structures and is an isomorphism on the pure parts. This predicts that the pure cohomological information of the tame character variety agrees with that of the corresponding open de Rham space; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
R036.source_name: Tamás Hausel, Michael Lennox Wong and Dimitri Wyss, “Arithmetic and metric aspects of open de Rham spaces”, arXiv:1807.04057 (2023).

R036.title: Irregular purity conjecture for wild character varieties
R036.statement:
Let $\mathscr{M}_{{\bm \mu},\mathbf r}^*$ be the open de Rham space of meromorphic connections with the prescribed regular and higher-order poles, and let $\mathscr{M}_{\mathbf B}^{{\bm\mu},\mathbf r}$ be the corresponding wild character variety. The irregular Riemann–Hilbert map is

$$
\nu:\mathscr{M}_{{\bm \mu},\mathbf r}^*\to\mathscr{M}_{\mathbf B}^{{\bm\mu},\mathbf r}.
$$

**Irregular purity conjecture.** The map $\nu$ induces

$$
\nu^*:H^*(\mathscr{M}_{\mathbf B}^{{\bm\mu},\mathbf r},\mathbb Q)\to H^*(\mathscr{M}_{{\bm\mu},\mathbf r}^*,\mathbb Q)
$$

which preserves mixed Hodge structures and is an isomorphism on the pure parts. This predicts purity compatibility between the wild character variety and the de Rham moduli space; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
R036.source_name: Tamás Hausel, Michael Lennox Wong and Dimitri Wyss, “Arithmetic and metric aspects of open de Rham spaces”, arXiv:1807.04057 (2023).

R036.title: Arithmeticity conjecture for isotropic transvections in mapping class group representations
R036.statement:
Let $(S,G)$ be in the situation of the corollary: for $\chi\in X(\mathbb{Q}G)$, assume that $\operatorname{\mathscr{X}}(S,G)$ has a nonzero image in $H_1(S;\mathbb{Q})_\chi$. For each $G$-orbit $A\in G\backslash\operatorname{\mathscr{X}}(S,G)$, let $T_A[\chi]$ denote the corresponding isotropic transvection, and let ${\mathscr M}{on}^\circ(S)[\chi]$ be the identity component of the Zariski closure of the representation.

**Arithmeticity conjecture.** The group generated by the isotropic transvections $\{T_A[\chi]\}_{A\in G\backslash\operatorname{\mathscr{X}}(S,G)}$ maps onto an arithmetic subgroup of ${\mathscr M}{on}^\circ(S)[\chi]$.

This conjecture concerns the arithmetic size of the subgroup generated by the geometric transvections. The source proposes it after proving that the relevant image spans $H_1(S;\mathbb{Q})_\chi$ and that the Zariski-closure identity component is $\mathbb{Q}$-almost simple; no resolution is given.
R036.source_name: Marco Boggi and Eduard Looijenga, “Curves with prescribed symmetry and associated representations of mapping class groups”, arXiv:1811.09741 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.09741

R036.title: The Eudave-Muñoz surgery characterization for Seifert graph manifolds
R036.statement:
Let $T_{a,b}$ and $T_{c,d}$ be nontrivial torus knots, and let $Y=Y(T_{a,b},T_{c,d})$. A surgery has **half-integral toroidal slope** when its slope is half-integral and the resulting manifold is toroidal. **Eudave-Muñoz surgery conjecture.** The manifold $Y$ is the result of $r$-surgery on a knot $K$ in $S^3$ if and only if $K$ is an Eudave-Muñoz knot and $r$ is its half-integral toroidal slope. In particular, one must have

$$
Y\cong \pm Y(T_{l,lm-1},T_{2,-(2m-1)})
$$

for some integers $l$ and $m$. This is presented as an expectation because the preceding theorem leaves five cases unresolved, and the authors do not know whether those cases can be realized as surgeries; the claim combines that expectation with the known non-integral obstruction.
R036.source_name: Steven Sivek and Raphael Zentner, “Surgery obstructions and character varieties”, arXiv:1912.01866 (2021).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01866

R036.title: Density conjecture for geometric-origin representations on special subschemes
R036.statement:
Let $X$ be a normal complex variety, let $x\in X(\mathbb C)$, and let $\pi=\pi_1(X(\mathbb C),x)$. Let

$$
Z\hookrightarrow {\rm Ch}_{\operatorname{GL}_r,\mathbb C}(\pi)
$$

be a special subscheme. A point of $Z$ is **of geometric origin** when it corresponds to a representation $\rho\colon \pi\to \operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$ whose associated local system is of geometric origin.

**Special-locus density conjecture.** The set of complex points of $Z$ corresponding to representations of geometric origin is dense in $Z$. In particular, the special points are dense on $Z$.

This extends the paper's density question from the full character variety to special, or arithmetic, subschemes. The source gives no resolution of this special-locus conjecture; it refers back to the obstruction showing that the unrestricted density conjecture is false in general.
R036.source_name: Hélène Esnault and Moritz Kerz, “Local systems with quasi-unipotent monodromy at infinity are dense”, arXiv:2101.00487 (2022).

R036.title: Looijenga's conjecture on the smooth Torelli group of Enriques surfaces
R036.statement:
Let $Y$ be an Enriques surface, and let $H^*(Y,\mathbb{Z})$ be its integral cohomology equipped with the quadratic form $Q_Y$. Define the **smooth Torelli group** by

$$
\mathcal{I}_Y:=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Mod}(Y)\to\operatorname{Aut}(H^*(Y,\mathbb{Z}),Q_Y)\bigr).
$$

**Looijenga's conjecture.** The smooth Torelli group is trivial:

$$
\mathcal{I}_Y=\{1\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether every mapping class of an Enriques surface that acts trivially on integral cohomology is itself trivial. It was suggested by Looijenga; the supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
R036.source_name: Sidhanth Raman, “A smooth Birman-Hilden theory for hyperkähler manifolds”, arXiv:2402.17047 (2025).

R036.title: Arithmetic-dynamic simplicity dichotomy for geodesics
R036.statement: Consider a lattice $F\subset \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with invariant trace field $\K=\mathbb{Q}(\{\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)\mid \gamma\in F\})$. Let $S=F\backslash\mathbb{H}$, with mapping class group $\operatorname{Mod}(S)=\operatorname{Out}(F)$. Fix a simple geodesic $\alpha\subset S$, let $\widetilde{\alpha}\subset\mathbb{H}$ be its lift, viewed as an $F$-invariant set of geodesics, and let $\partial\widetilde{\alpha}\subset\mathbb{R}\mathbb{P}^1$ be the set of their endpoints. **Arithmetic-dynamic simplicity conjecture.** The following dichotomy holds: if $\alpha$ is fixed by an element of infinite order in $\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, then the endpoints in $\partial\widetilde{\alpha}$ are algebraic over $\K$; if $\alpha$ is not fixed by any element of infinite order in $\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, then the endpoints in $\partial\widetilde{\alpha}$ are transcendental over $\K$. In the first case, the relevant algebraic extension is further determined by the type of infinite-order mapping class: for a maximal product of commuting Dehn twists, the lifted geodesics are bi-asymptotic to simple closed geodesics and their endpoints lie in a quadratic extension of $\K$; for a pseudo-Anosov element $A\in\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, the endpoints are expected to belong to $\K[\mu_j]$ for a Lyapunov exponent $\mu_j$ given by a root of the Teichmüller polynomial of $A$. This proposes an arithmetic/transcendence dichotomy for simple geodesics, relating the algebraicity of their endpoints to dynamical symmetries of the surface. The general status is not supplied in the source.
R036.source_name: Scott Schmieding and Christopher-Lloyd Simon, “Geometry and Transcendence of the Hexponential”, arXiv:2402.17628 (2024).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17628

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

R036.title: Potential density of integral points in relative character varieties
R036.statement:
Let $Y$ be a smooth complex variety equipped with a smooth projective simple normal crossings compactification $\overline{Y}$, and let $D=\overline{Y}\setminus Y$ have components $D_1,\ldots,D_n$. Let $G$ be a Chevalley group over $\mathbb{Z}$, let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathscr{O}_K$, and let $X_{G,\underline{C}}(Y)$ denote the relative character variety of representations of $\pi_1(Y)$ into $G$ whose local monodromy around each $D_i$ has prescribed image $C_i$ in $(G/_{\operatorname{ad}}G)(\mathscr{O}_K)$, where $\underline{C}=(C_i)_{i=1,\ldots,n}$. Fix

$$
\underline{C}\in (G/_{\operatorname{ad}}G)(\mathscr{O}_K)^n.
$$

**Potential-density conjecture.** Integral points are potentially Zariski-dense in the $K$-scheme $X_{G,\underline{C}}(Y)_K$: there exists a finite extension $L/K$ such that the Zariski closure of the $\mathscr{O}_L$-points of $X_{G,\underline{C}}(Y)$ contains $X_{G,\underline{C}}(Y)_K$.

The conjecture predicts arithmetic largeness of relative character varieties with fixed boundary monodromy, generalizing the paper's evidence from the case of $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and using a reduction to Riemann surfaces together with mapping-class-group dynamics. Its general validity for Chevalley groups and arbitrary smooth quasi-projective varieties remains open.
R036.source_name: Simone Coccia and Daniel Litt, “Density of integral points in the Betti moduli of quasi-projective varieties”, arXiv:2507.00167 (2025).
R036.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2404.17185](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17185), [arXiv:math/0410558](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410558).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

R036.title: Existence conjecture for LMO-trivial manifolds in the Johnson filtration
R036.statement:
Let $\mathcal{I}_g$ be the Torelli group, let $\mathcal{I}_g(k)$ be its $k$th Johnson-filtration subgroup, and let $M_{\phi}$ denote the integral homology 3-sphere constructed from a mapping class $\phi$. **Existence of LMO-trivial manifolds.** For every integer $k\geq 1$, there may exist a non-trivial mapping class $\phi_k\in\mathcal{I}_g(k)$ such that

$$
\hat{Z}_{\mathrm{LMO}}(M_{\phi_k})=\hat{Z}_{\mathrm{LMO}}(S^3).
$$

Such manifolds would be invisible to the classical LMO invariant and would refute classical LMO completeness. The supplied text presents this as a proposed mechanism and gives no resolution.
R036.source_name: Takahito Kuriya, “The LMO Spectrum: Factorization Homology and the E_3-Structure of the Jacobi Diagram Algebra”, arXiv:2508.18985 (2025).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18985

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

R036.title: Ivanov's conjecture on finite-index subgroups of mapping class groups
R036.statement: Let $S_g^n$ be a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g^n)$ be its mapping class group. Let $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{Mod}(S_g^n)$ be a finite-index subgroup, and write $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}$ for its abelianization and $H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{Z})$ for its first integral cohomology. **Ivanov's conjecture.** For $g\geq 3$ and $n\geq 0$, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}=H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{Z})$ is finite. This is a central finite-abelianization conjecture for finite-index subgroups of mapping class groups. The paper notes substantial partial results and the relation to the Putman–Wieland conjecture, but does not state a resolution in the supplied text.
R036.source_name: Pierre Godfard, “Rigidity of SU(2) and SO(3) quantum representations of mapping class groups at prime levels”, arXiv:2511.19795 (2025).
R036.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19795

R036.title: Constant-order structure conjecture for Reshetikhin–Turaev theory
R036.statement:
Let $p$ be a fixed prime with $p\geq 3$. Let ${\cal V}^I_p$ denote the integral TQFT, and let $\dov {\cal V}^{FN}_p$ denote the corresponding Fibonacci-type TQFT; the tensor product is taken $\frac{p-3}{2}$ times. **Constant-order structure conjecture.** The irreducible components of ${\cal V}^I_p$ can be found as irreducible components of

$$
\bigotimes^{\frac{p-3}{2}}\dov {\cal V}^{FN}_p.
$$

This conjecture concerns a proposed polynomial dependence between the integral and Fibonacci-type Reshetikhin–Turaev theories, motivated by the corresponding relation between their asymptotic dimension growth rates. The authors note that it can be verified for the genus-one mapping class group, whose representation is ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$; its status in general is not specified here.
R036.source_name: Thomas Kerler, “Resolutions of p-Modular TQFT's and Representations of Symmetric Groups”, arXiv:math/0110006 (2002).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0110006

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2001).

R036.title: The p-modular TQFT structure conjecture
R036.statement:
Let $p\geq 5$ be a prime and let

$$
q_p=\frac{p-3}{2}.
$$

Let $\Gamma_g$ denote the mapping class group of a genus-$g$ surface, let $\dov{\cal U}^{(k)}_p$ be the $p$-modular TQFTs extending the $\Gamma_g$-representations arising from the short exact sequences in the Johnson–Morita extension, let ${\cal V}_p^{[\leq 0]}$ be the reduced TQFT over $\mathbb F_p$, and let ${\cal V}_{\zeta_p}^I$ be the integral Reshetikhin–Turaev TQFT over $\mathbb Z[\zeta_p]$. A TQFT is **half-projective** with parameter ${\sf x}$ if its composition law is modified by a factor ${\sf x}^{\mu(C_2,C_1)}$, where $\mu(C_2,C_1)$ is the rank of the connecting map in the relevant Mayer–Vietoris sequence.

**The p-modular TQFT structure conjecture.**

A) There are TQFTs $\dov{\cal U}^{(k)}_p$ which extend the $\Gamma_g$-representations from the Johnson–Morita extension.

B) The TQFT ${\cal V}_p^{[\leq 0]}$ over $\mathbb F_p$ is a quotient of sub-TQFTs of the $q_p$-fold symmetric product $\operatorname{S}^{q_p}\dov{\cal U}^{(1)}_p$.

C) The TQFT ${\cal V}_{\zeta_p}^I$ is half-projective with parameter ${\sf x}=(\zeta_p-1)^{q_p}$ and consequently has a block-structured $\mathbb Z[\zeta_p]$-basis.

The three assertions are related: B depends on A, while the block structure in C is intended to imply half-projectivity. The conjecture describes the structure of the $p$-modular and integral TQFTs and their relation to mapping class group representations; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
R036.source_name: Thomas Kerler, “p-Modular TQFT's, Milnor torsion and the Casson-Lescop invariant”, arXiv:math/0203256 (2002).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203256

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2002).

R036.title: Exact-sequence conjecture relating homology-cylinder filtrations
R036.statement:
Let $H$ be the first homology group used to define the tree and homology-cylinder filtrations, and let $\mathcal G_k^Y(\mathcal H_g)$ and $\mathcal G_k^w(\mathcal H_g)$ denote their degree-$k$ graded groups. For $k>1$, write $k=2l$ or $k=2l-1$ as appropriate. **Exact-sequence conjecture.** For $l>1$, the relationship between these graded groups should be given by the exact sequences

$$
0\longrightarrow \mathcal G_{2l}^Y(\mathcal H_g)\longrightarrow \mathcal G_{2l}^w(\mathcal H_g)\longrightarrow L_{l+1}(H)/2L_{l+1}(H)\longrightarrow 0
$$

and

$$
H\otimes L_l(H)/2L_l(H)\longrightarrow \mathcal G_{2l-1}^Y(\mathcal H_g)\longrightarrow \mathcal G_{2l-1}^w(\mathcal H_g)\longrightarrow 0.
$$

These sequences are proposed as the precise comparison between the two filtrations, incorporating the preceding conjectures. The source provides related rational and torsion exact sequences, but does not establish these sharper integral sequences.
R036.source_name: Jerome Levine, “Addendum and correction to: Homology cylinders: an enlargement of the mapping class group”, arXiv:math/0207290 (2002).
R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207290

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2002).

R036.title: Tangent-cone conjecture for moduli space
R036.statement:
Let $\M_g$ be moduli space with the Teichmüller metric, and let ${\cal C}_g$ be the curve complex of a closed genus-$g$ surface: its vertices are nontrivial, nonperipheral isotopy classes of simple closed curves, with simplices given by collections admitting mutually disjoint representatives. Define the tangent cone at infinity by

$$
\operatorname{cone}(\M_g):=\lim_{n\to\infty}(\M_g,\tfrac1n d_{\rm Teich}),
$$

with pointed Gromov–Hausdorff convergence. **Tangent-cone conjecture for moduli space.**

$$
\operatorname{cone}(\M_g)\text{ is homeomorphic to the open cone on }{\cal C}_g/{\rm Mod}_g.
$$

The source notes that the precise formulation requires orbi-complexes and that related arithmetic-lattice analogues are known; the stated moduli-space identification remains conjectural.

R036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606432

R036.title: Stable cohomology of character varieties
R036.statement:
Prove (or disprove) that the cohomology of $\mathcal{U}_{G,g}$ stabilizes with respect to $g$ and compute its stable value.

A conjecture for the value of the putative stable cohomology should include Chern classes. Does it depend on anything else? What about integral cohomology?
R036.source_name: AimPL: Motives and mapping class groups (posed by Aaron Landesman)

R036.title: Decidability of arithmeticity and motivicty
R036.statement: Let $X / \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth projective variety. Is there an algorithm which given an integral point of the character variety $x \in M_B(X, r)(\mathcal{O}_K)$, where $K$ is a number field, can decide if $x$ is (after some embedding $\mathcal{O}_K \subset \mathbb{Q}_p$) an arithmetic local system? Likewise, is there an algorithm to determine if $x$ arises from geometry?

R036.title: Predictions of the Relative Fontaine-Mazur and Simpson conjectures (problem 3)
R036.statement: Let $X / \mathbb{F}_q$ be a smooth projective variety over a finite field. Given a representation $\rho: \pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}_q}}, \bar{x}) \to \mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb{Z}_{\ell})$ (perhaps specified via an oracle returning its action on $(\mathbb{Z} / \ell^n \mathbb{Z})^r$ for each $n$ which is itself equivalent to the data of a certain finite etale cover and hence specified by a finite amount of data) is there an algorithm which decides if $\rho$ is arithmetic (equivalently motivic).

R036.title: Unstable cohomology
R036.statement:
Let $c$ be a union of conjugacy classes in a group $G$.
What can we say about the Frobenius action on the cohomology of
$\operatorname{Hur}^c_n$?
What can we say about top degree cohomology?
Can one compute $H_{n-1}(\operatorname{Hur}^c_n)$?
Can we use the fact that the Braid group is a duality group?
What should we even conjecture about the Frobenius action to be consistent with
arithmetic applications? What would give the expected arithmetic results?
Some of these questions may also be applicable when $c$ is, more generally, a
rack.

Aaron Landesman and Ishan Levy have proven an exponential lower bound via
private communication (but this has not been written anywhere). 
Separately, there is an exponential upper bound with a
larger exponent. For the specific classes that are easiest to construct, one may
be able to understand the Frobenius action. This is a free Lie algebra.

Jordan Ellenberg comments it would be interesting to compute the trace of
Frobenius on this.
Separately, it would also be interesting to understand what representations of
the mapping class group show up in this cohomology?

Craig Westerland points out the entirety of the top homology is the primitives
in the shuffle algebra.
If one lets $G$ range over all groups, this limits toward a faithful
representation of 
a certain group ring,
even just for the Hurwitz spaces on
$3$ points.
This has something to do with Belyi's theorem.

Jeremy Miller was interested in understanding the top
degree cohomology associated to a Burau representation.
Dan Petersen thinks that there will be a lot of cohomology in the top degree
associated to Burau representations.
R036.source_name: AimPL: Moments in families of L-functions over function fields (posed by Jeremy Miller)

R036.title: Question 2.1 — (Ends spectrum).
R036.statement: (Ends spectrum). What are the possibile values of ends(Modg,H ) for finitely- generated subgroups H <Modg? It is well-known that the moduli space Mg has one end. The key point of the proof is that the complex of curves is connected. This proof actually gives more: any cover of Mg has one end; see, e.g., [ FMa]. However, I do not see how this fact directly gives information about Question 2.1. Commensurators. Asking for two subgroups of a group to be conjugate is often too restrictive a question. A more robust notion is that of commensurability. Subgroups Γ 1, Γ2 of a group H are commensurable if there exists h ∈ H such that hΓ1h−1∩ Γ2 has finite index in both hΓ1h−1 and in Γ 2. One then wants to classify subgroups up to commensurability; this is the natural equivalence relation one studies in order to coarsify the relation of “conjugate” to ignore finite index information. The primary commensurability invariant for subgroups Γ < H is the commensurator of Γ in H, denoted Comm H (Γ), defined as: CommH (Γ):= {h∈H:hΓh−1∩ Γ has finite index in both Γ and hΓh−1} The commensurator has most commonly been studied for discrete subgroups of Lie groups. One of the most striking results about commensurators, due to Margulis, states that if Γ is an irreducible lattice in a semisimple 2 Lie group H then [Comm H (Γ): Γ] = ∞ if and only if Γ is arithmetic. In other words, it is precisely the arithmetic lattices that have infinitely many “hidden symmetries”. 2By semisimple we will always mean linear semisimple with no compact factors. 16 B. Farb
R036.source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

R036.title: Problem 2.16 — (Automorphism groups with special properties).
R036.statement: (Automorphism groups with special properties). LetP be a property of finite groups, for example being nilpotent, solvable, or a p-group. R036.title: Problem 3.6 — (Generalized word problem).
R036.statement: (Generalized word problem). Determine the subgroups H in Modg for which the generalized word problem is solvable. Give eﬃcient algorithms to solve the generalized word problem for these subgroups. Find the optimal time bounds for such algorithms. Of course this problem is too broad to solve in complete generality; results even in special cases might be interesting. Some solutions to Problem 3.6 are given by Leininger-McReynolds 26 B. Farb in [ LM]. We also note that Bridson-Miller (personal communication), extending an old result of Baumslag-Roseblade, have proven that any product of finite rank free groups has solvable generalized word problem with respect to any finitely presented subgroup. In light of this result, it would be interesting to determine whether or not there is a finitely presented subgroup of Mod g with respect to which the generalized word problem is not solvable. Distortion and quasiconvexity. There is a refinement of Problem 3.6. Let H be a finitely generated subgroup of a finitely generated group Γ. Fix finite generating sets on both H and Γ. This choice gives a word metric on both H and Γ, where dΓ(g,h ) is defined to be the minimal number of generators of Γ needed to represent gh−1. Let N denote the natural numbers. We say that a function f: N−→ N is a distortion function for H in Γ if for every word w in the generators of Γ, if w represents an element w∈H then dH (1,w)≤f (dΓ(1,w)) In this case we also say that “ H has distortion f (n) in Γ.” It is easy to see that the growth type of f, i.e. polynomial, exponential, etc., does not depend on the choice of generators for either H or Γ. It is also easy to see that f (n) is constant if and only if H is finite; otherwise f is at least linear. It is proved in [ F a1] that, for a group Γ with solvable word problem, the distortion of H in Γ is recursive if and only if H has solvable generalized word problem in Γ. For some concrete examples, we note that the center of the 3-dimensional integral Heisenberg group has quadratic distortion; and the cyclic group generated by b in the group ⟨a,b: aba−1 = b2⟩ has exponential distortion since anba−n =b2n.

For many arithmetic groups Γ the conjecture can be proved by combining some well-known information about arithmetic groups with equally well-known properties of Mod S. R037.title: Saxl's 2-modular tensor-square conjecture
R037.statement:
Let $\Bbbk$ be a field of characteristic $2$, let $n=k(k+1)/2$, and let $\rho(k)=(k,k-1,\dots,2,1)$. A partition is **2-regular** if no positive part occurs at least twice, and ${\bf D}^\Bbbk(\lambda)$ denotes the corresponding simple $\Bbbk\mathfrak{S}_n$-module. **Saxl's 2-modular conjecture.** For every 2-regular partition $\lambda$ of $n$, 
$$
\dim_\Bbbk\left(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}\left({\bf D}^\Bbbk(\rho(k))\otimes {\bf D}^\Bbbk(\rho(k)),{\bf D}^\Bbbk(\lambda)\right)\right)>0.
$$
 Equivalently, the tensor square contains all indecomposable projective modules as direct summands with positive multiplicity. This extends the verified complex staircase positivity statement to characteristic $2$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

R037.title: The staircase-weight multiplicity-free converse conjecture
R037.statement: Suppose $w\in{\mathfrak S}_n$ and $I\subseteq J(w)$. Let $D=[n-1]\setminus I$, and let $\lambda^{\mathrm{staircase}}=(n,n-1,\ldots,3,2,1)$. Write $\kappa_\beta$ for the relevant character and say that it is **$D$-multiplicity-free** when its decomposition has no repeated multiplicities. **The staircase-weight multiplicity-free converse conjecture.** If $X_w$ is $L_I$-spherical, then $\kappa_{w\lambda^{\mathrm{staircase}}}$ is $D$-multiplicity-free. The preceding corollary proves the contrapositive implication; the conjecture would make that criterion an equivalence and reduce an infinite family of checks to one staircase weight. R037.title: Saxl's staircase tensor-square conjecture
R037.statement:
For $k\geq 1$, let

$$
\delta_k=(k,k-1,\ldots,1)
$$

be the staircase partition, which has size $\binom{k+1}{2}$. For partitions of this size, $g(\delta_k,\delta_k,\mu)$ is the multiplicity of the irreducible $S_{\binom{k+1}{2}}$-module indexed by $\mu$ in the tensor square of the module indexed by $\delta_k$.

**Saxl's conjecture.**

$$
g(\delta_k,\delta_k,\mu)>0
$$

for all $k$ and all $\mu\vdash\binom{k+1}{2}$.

This is a concrete proposed choice of the symmetric partition in the tensor square conjecture. Its significance is that the staircase partition is specified uniformly rather than existentially.

R037.title: Hopkins's rowmotion cyclic sieving meta-conjecture
R037.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite graded poset of rank $r$ for which the roots of $\aΩ_P(m)$ are all integers or half-integers, and in the latter case possessing an order two automorphism. Let $m \a0geq 1$ be an integer and define

$$
\Omega_P(m;q):= \prod_{\alpha} \frac{1-q^{\kappa(m-\alpha)}}{1-q^{-\kappa \alpha}},
$$

a product over all the roots $\alpha$ of $\Omega_P(m)$ with multiplicity, and with $\kappa:= 1$ if the roots are integers or $\kappa:= 2$ if they are half-integers. **Hopkins's rowmotion cyclic sieving meta-conjecture.** Then $\Omega_P(m;q)$ is a polynomial in $q$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and

$$
(\mathcal{PP}^m(P),\langle \mathrm{Row} \rangle \simeq \mathbb{Z}/\kappa(r+2)\mathbb{Z},\Omega_P(m;q))
$$

exhibits cyclic sieving. This predicts a uniform cyclic sieving phenomenon for rowmotion on $P$-partitions; the paper recalls several proved families and establishes the staircase case, while the general assertion remains open.

R038.title: Negative type conjecture for 3-subdivisions of graphs with a $K_{2,3}$ minor
R038.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph containing $K_{2,3}$ as a minor, and let the $3$-subdivision of $G$ be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of $G$ three times. Equip it with its shortest path metric.

**Negative type conjecture.** There is no graph $G$ with a $K_{2,3}$ minor where the shortest distance metric of the $3$-subdivision of $G$ has negative type.

This conjecture proposes that the obstruction to negative type established for sufficiently fine subdivisions already occurs for the $3$-subdivision. R039.title: Furstenberg–Kesten conjecture on bigeodesics in two-dimensional first-passage percolation
R039.statement: Let $(t_e)$ be i.i.d. edge weights on the nearest-neighbor edges of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, with a continuous distribution. A **bigeodesic** is a doubly infinite path whose finite segments are geodesics for the induced passage-time metric. **Furstenberg–Kesten's bigeodesic conjecture.** Almost surely, there are no bigeodesics in dimension two. R040.title: The Unification Conjecture for mutual free information and free entropy
R040.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be self-adjoint operators in a $\mathrm{II}_1$-factor $(\mathscr{A},\tau)$, such that $\chi(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, $\chi(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$, and $\chi(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ are all finite.

**Unification Conjecture.** The mutual free information satisfies

$$
i^\ast(W^\ast(x_1,\ldots,x_n):W^\ast(y_1,\ldots,y_n))=-\chi(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n)+\chi(x_1,\ldots,x_n)+\chi(y_1,\ldots,y_n).
$$

This is part of the broader question of whether the microstates and non-microstates free entropies agree in general. The source states that both this identity and $\chi=\chi^\ast$ are unknown, so the conjecture remains open.

R041.title: Saroglou's three-dimensional ellipsoid conjecture for a section functional

R041.title: Saroglou's lower-bound conjecture for the second projection body
R041.statement:
Let $K$ be a $d$-dimensional convex body containing the origin in its interior. Define

$$
m(K):=\min_{x\in S^{d-1}}\frac{h_{\Pi^2K}(x)}{h_K(x)V(K)^{d-2}}.
$$

For $x\in S^{d-1}$, let $K\cap(sx+x^\bot)$ be the $(d-1)$-dimensional section and let $V_{d-1}$ denote its volume. **Saroglou's lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
m(K)\geq\max_{x\in S^{d-1}}\omega_{d-2}^{d-1}\omega_{d-1}^{3-d}\left\{\frac{\left(\displaystyle\int_{-h_K(x)}^{h_K(x)}V_{d-1}\left(K\cap(sx+x^\bot)\right)^{\frac{d-2}{d-1}}ds\right)^{d-1}}{h_K(x)V(K)^{d-2}}\right\}.
$$

The source presents this as a conjectural all-dimensional strengthening related to its proved three-dimensional lower-bound results; no resolution is given.
R041.source_name: Christos Saroglou, “On the shape of a convex body with respect to its second projection body”, arXiv:1409.4347 (2014).
R041.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

R041.title: Saroglou's lower-order projection-body minimizer conjecture
R041.statement:
Let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $i=1,\dots,d-1$, define the order-$i$ projection body $\Pi_iK$ using the mixed projection-body construction, and set

$$
P_i(K):=\frac{V(\Pi_iK)}{V(K)^i},\qquad Q_i(K):=\frac{V\big(\Pi_i(\Pi K)\big)}{V(K)^{i(d-1)}}.
$$

**Saroglou's lower-order projection-body conjecture.** For $i=1,\dots,d-2$, the functionals $P_i(\cdot)$ and $Q_i(\cdot)$ are minimized precisely for Euclidean balls. The source notes that the $i=d-1$ case of $P_i$ is Petty's conjecture and that this statement is open; it also identifies the $Q_1$ case as a conjecture of Maresch and Schuster.
R041.source_name: Christos Saroglou, “On the shape of a convex body with respect to its second projection body”, arXiv:1409.4347 (2014).
R041.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

R041.title: Petty's polar projection problem
R041.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be an $o$-symmetric convex body, and let $\Pi K$ be its projection body, defined by

$$
h_{\Pi K}(u)=\operatorname{vol}_{n-1}(K\mid u^\perp),\qquad u\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}.
$$

Its polar projection body is $\Pi^\circ K=(\Pi K)^\circ$. **Petty's conjecture.** If $n\geq 3$ and $\Pi^\circ K=\lambda K$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, then $K$ is an ellipsoid. This polar projection problem is a classical question in convex geometry; the stated version is known for convex polytopes, where Martini proved that the only such polytopes are simplices, but the general problem remains open.
R041.source_name: Ákos G. Horváth and Zsolt Lángi, “On the convex hull and homothetic convex hull functions of a convex body”, arXiv:2012.08955 (2021).
R041.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1511.03381](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03381), [arXiv:1305.1437](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.1437).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08955

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2020). “This version was settled by Martini in for convex polytopes, who proved, using an elegant argument, that the only convex polytopes with the above property are the simplices.”

R041.title: Shape of the ground state
R041.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded convex set, and let $u$ be the lowest eigenfunction (ground state) of the Laplacian with Dirichet boundary conditions, with unit $L^2$ norm. A general question is to relate the domain $\Omega$ and the ground state $u$ with a rectangular domain $R$ associated to a ground state with separated variables.

For this we introduce the following notations: let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be a unit vector ($|\xi|=1$). Let 

$$
P(\xi)=\int_{\partial \Omega} |\xi \cdot \nabla u|^2 \, dS, \qquad Q(\xi)=\int_\Omega |\xi \cdot \nabla u|^2 \, dx.
$$

%\color{blue}It is known that $Q$ is the projection body function for volume.

It is known that 

$$
Q(\Omega) \leq \frac{c}{\text{inradius}(\Omega)^2}.
$$

A first question is the relation between $P$ and $Q$: the first is linked to the shape derivative of $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ in the direction of $\xi$, while the second is related to the distribution of $\nabla u $ in $\Omega$.

A second question is whether $\log(u)$ is “essentially quadratic” on the interior of $\Omega$ in the following sense: it is known that $\log(u)$ is concave and reaches a unique maximum at some point $p^*$, the conjecture raised by David Jerison is whether there exists some constant $C_n>0$ such that for any $p\in \{u>\frac{1}{2}u(p^*)\}$, we have

$$
\frac{1}{C_n}\left(-\nabla^2 \log\ u(p)\right)\leq \left(-\nabla^2\log\ u(p^*)\right)\leq C_n\left(-\nabla^2\log\ u(p)\right).
$$
R041.source_name: AimPL: Symmetry-breaking of optimal shapes (posed by David Jerison)

R041.title: Petty’s conjectured projection inequality
R041.statement:
For every dimension $d\ge 3$, let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Define its projection body by $h_{\Pi K}(x)=\lvert K\mid x^\perp\rvert$ for $x\in S^{d-1}$, where $K\mid x^\perp$ is the orthogonal projection of $K$ onto $x^\perp$, and set
$$
P(K):=\frac{\lvert\Pi K\rvert}{\lvert K\rvert^{d-1}}.
$$
Conjecture: $P(K)$ is minimal if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid.

D32.title: The parameter-boundary conjecture for the reverse Mittag–Leffler inequality
D32.statement:
Let $E_{\alpha,\beta}$ be the two-parameter Mittag–Leffler function. A **complete Bernstein function** is understood in the standard sense, and consider the global reverse inequality

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{C}.
$$

**The parameter-boundary conjecture.** There exists an increasing convex function $f:[2,\infty)\to[3,\infty)$ with $f(2)=3$ such that, for every $\alpha\ge2$,

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\ \text{globally}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\log E_{\alpha,\beta}\ \text{is a complete Bernstein function}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\beta\le f(\alpha).
$$

At $\alpha=2$ the corresponding boundary is known to be $f(2)=3$, and the paper gives partial support for extending this description to $\alpha>2$. The conjecture also predicts monotonicity and convexity of the boundary separating the parameter regions.
D32.source_name: Roberto Garrappa, Stefan Gerhold, Marina Popolizio and Thomas Simon, “On some inequalities for the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function in the complex plane”, arXiv:2410.11852 (2025).
D32.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11852

D37.title: Gromov's surface subgroup conjecture for one-ended hyperbolic groups
D37.statement: Let $G$ be a one-ended word-hyperbolic group, meaning a word-hyperbolic group with one end. Let the surface group of genus $2$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $2$. **Gromov's conjecture.** The group $G$ contains an embedded copy of the surface group of genus $2$. If true, together with the inheritance of domino-problem undecidability by groups containing suitable subgroups, this would imply undecidability for every one-ended word-hyperbolic group. The conjecture is presented in the source without a resolution.
D37.source_name: Nathalie Aubrun, Sebastián Barbieri and Etienne Moutot, “The domino problem is undecidable on surface groups”, arXiv:1811.08420 (2018).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.08420

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

D37.title: Primality characterization for polyomino ideals without zig-zag walks
D37.statement:
Let ${\mathcal P}$ be a polyomino. Its **polyomino ideal** $I_{\mathcal P}$ is the ideal associated with ${\mathcal P}$, and a **zig-zag walk** is a walk in ${\mathcal P}$ of the type described in the paper.

**Primality conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. The polyomino ideal $I_{\mathcal P}$ is prime.
2. ${\mathcal P}$ contains no zig-zag walks.

This conjecture proposes a complete combinatorial characterization of the primality of polyomino ideals, extending the paper's results for polyominoes containing zig-zag walks, polyominoes of rank at most $14$, and grid polyominoes. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
D37.source_name: Carla Mascia, Giancarlo Rinaldo and Francesco Romeo, “Primality of multiply connected polyominoes”, arXiv:1907.08438 (2020).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08438

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

D37.title: Levelness conjecture for simple thin path polyominoes with singleton maximal intervals
D37.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple thin polyomino, meaning a path polyomino with no interval containing more than two cells, and suppose that every maximal interval consists of a single cell. Let $S/I_{\mathcal{P}}$ be the quotient by the associated polyomino ideal. **Levelness conjecture.** The ring $S/I_{\mathcal{P}}$ is level. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that the path polyominoes covered by the preceding theorem have at least one single cell in every interval, together with computational evidence; its general validity remains open.
D37.source_name: Giancarlo Rinaldo, Francesco Romeo and Rajib Sarkar, “Level and pseudo-Gorenstein path polyominoes”, arXiv:2308.05461 (2023).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05461

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

D37.title: Behrend–Fischer–Koutschan symmetry conjecture for off-diagonally symmetric ASMs
D37.statement:
Let $\text{OSASM}(2n)$ denote the set of off-diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices of order $2n$. For $X\in\text{OSASM}(2n)$, let $\mathsf{R}(X)$ be the number of nonzero strictly upper-triangular entries and let $\mathsf{T}(X)$ be the column containing the $1$ in the first row. Define

$$
S(2n;\rho,\tau)=\{X\in\text{OSASM}(2n):\mathsf{R}(X)=\rho,\mathsf{T}(X)=\tau\}.
$$

**Behrend–Fischer–Koutschan symmetry conjecture.** Given $n$, for any $\rho$ and $\tau$, we have

$$
|S(2n;\rho,\tau)|=|S(2n;\rho,2n+2-\tau)|.
$$

This conjecture asserts a reflection symmetry in the refined enumeration of off-diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices according to the number of nonzero strictly upper-triangular entries and the position of the first-row $1$. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
D37.source_name: Yi-Lin Lee, “Off-diagonally symmetric domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of odd order”, arXiv:2404.09057 (2024).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

D37.title: Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo primality conjecture for polyomino ideals
D37.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a polyomino, and let $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ be its polyomino ideal. A **zig–zag walk** is the combinatorial configuration defined earlier in the source. The rank of $\mathcal{P}$ is the number of its cells.

**Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ is a prime ideal.
2. $\mathcal{P}$ contains no zig–zag walk.

The equivalence is known for polyominoes of rank at most $14$, based on systematic enumeration and computation. The conjecture asserts that the zig–zag obstruction is the only obstruction to primality in arbitrary rank.
D37.source_name: Francesco Navarra and Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, “Recent Advances in the Theory of Polyomino Ideals”, arXiv:2511.22778 (2025).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22778

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

D37.title: Mascia et al.'s primality conjecture for polyominoes
D37.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a polyomino. A polyomino is **prime** when its inner 2-minors ideal is prime, and a **zig-zag walk** is the configuration referred to in the source; every prime polyomino contains no zig-zag walk.

**Mascia et al.'s conjecture.** $\mathcal{P}$ is prime if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ contains no zig-zag walk.

The conjecture would give a characterization of primality for polyominoes. The forward implication is known, while the converse is presented as conjectural; its general status is open.
D37.source_name: Hong Wang and Jin Guo, “A class of polyocollection ideals with quadratic Gröbner bases”, arXiv:2607.22108 (2026).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

D37.title: Local lozenge probability conjecture for boxed plane partitions
D37.statement: Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the normalized side lengths of a hexagon, let $(x,y)$ be a normalized location in this hexagon, and let $\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}(x,y)$ denote the limiting density of vertical lozenges there. Let $V$ be any open set in the hexagon containing the four points at which $\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}$ is discontinuous. **Local lozenge probability conjecture.** As the scaling factor $\sigma\to\infty$, the probability of finding a vertical lozenge at normalized location $(x,y)\notin V$ is $\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}(x,y)+o(1)$, with the $o(1)$ error bound uniform for $(x,y)\notin V$. This conjecture concerns local statistics that are not determined by the paper's macroscopic averaging theorem; numerical evidence and analogous results for domino tilings support it, but it remains unproved here.
D37.source_name: Henry Cohn, Michael Larsen and James Propp, “The shape of a typical boxed plane partition”, arXiv:math/9801059 (2002).
D37.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9801059

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 1998).

D37.title: A conjecture on polyominoes and inscribed squares
D37.statement: Let $P$ be a polyomino with boundary a closed Jordan curve $J$. Assume that $P$ is built from unit squares with vertices at lattice points. Let the greatest open square $OS$, with horizontal and vertical sides, contained in the bounded component of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus J$ have sidelength $s$ (clearly an integer). Then $J$ contains four lattice points forming the vertices of a square $S$ of sidelength at least $s/\sqrt{2}$ if $s$ is even, and at least $\sqrt{m^2+(m+1)^2}$ if $s=2m+1$.
